ideas.truth: On a long transit day, the one thing that has to work without thought is the bag holding everything you need — that's the whole relief.
ideas.moment: A traveler drops onto a terminal bench beside a glowing DELAYED departures board, backpack still on one shoulder, and exhales as they finally let it slide off.
ideas.key_frame: Traveler seated on a wood bench, backpack half-off one shoulder, a blurred amber DELAYED sign glowing behind them in a dim terminal at dusk.

ideas.truth: The long way home — the layover, the delay, the red-eye — is where a traveler actually lets their guard down.
ideas.moment: The traveler dozes against the backpack on a moving night train, head resting on the strap, city lights sliding past the window.
ideas.key_frame: Traveler asleep against the backpack in a train seat, blurred neon city lights streaking the dark window behind them.

ideas.truth: Home isn't a place you land, it's the version of yourself that walks out steady after a hard journey.
ideas.moment: The traveler strides off the train straight into a new city at dusk, backpack settled on both shoulders, not breaking stride.
ideas.key_frame: Traveler mid-stride out of a station exit into a lit-up street at dusk, backpack on both shoulders, city glowing ahead.

why: The three moments form one continuous transit-day arc — tension, trust, arrival — with the traveler visible as the hero throughout and the exact reference-photo backpack anchoring every beat. A single closing still (matching the customer's poster brief) carries the headline, product name, URL and logo, so the same asset works as a short film AND exports cleanly as the 1:1/4:5 poster.
treatment: We open on a dim, wood-panelled transit terminal at dusk, a DELAYED board glowing amber in the background. The traveler drops onto a bench, backpack sliding off one shoulder — the first real exhale of the day. Cut to a night train: the same traveler dozes against the pack, head on the strap, city lights streaking the window — trust, not vigilance. Cut to a station exit at dusk: the traveler strides out into a lit street, pack settled on both shoulders, not breaking stride. Hard cut to the closing card: the exact Transit Backpack alone on the bench in warm rim-light, silhouette clean, with the headline, product name and URL in a calm shadowed band, logo at the base — the poster frame, in both 1:1 and 4:5.

scenes.prompt: A traveler wearing the exact Transit Backpack shown in the reference photos drops onto a worn wooden bench in a dim, wood-panelled transit terminal at dusk, letting the pack slide off one shoulder as they exhale. A backlit amber-glowing DEPARTURES board reading DELAYED sits soft-focus behind them. Warm light rims the bag's edge; background figures and platform lights fall into bokeh. Cinematic amber-and-charcoal palette, handheld stillness, with only the bag's own hardware visible as identifying detail.
scenes.first_frame_still_prompt: A tired traveler is caught mid-motion lowering onto a worn wooden bench, the exact reference Transit Backpack still hanging half-off one shoulder, straps loose, in a dim wood-panelled transit terminal at dusk. Behind them, a backlit amber DEPARTURES board glowing with the word DELAYED sits soft-focus, warm light rimming the bag's edge as scattered figures and platform lights blur into bokeh.
scenes.S1_feeling: Held tension — the fatigue of a delay finally catching up.
scenes.S2_first_frame: Traveler just touching down on the bench, pack still half-worn, delay board glowing behind — a story already in motion.
scenes.S3_one_action: One continuous action: sitting down and letting the backpack slide off one shoulder with an exhale.
scenes.S4_new_information: Establishes the traveler as hero, the obstacle (delay), and the product on their body, all at once.
scenes.S5_impact: A recognizable, specific transit-fatigue moment reads instantly, even at a glance on a phone feed.

scenes.prompt: The same traveler, on a moving night train, dozes against the exact Transit Backpack from the reference photos, head resting on its top strap. Blurred neon city lights stream past the dark window behind them. Slow, subtle push-in on the frame as the train gently rocks. Warm-cool contrast between skin-tone cabin light and cool window streaks. The bag's own hardware is the only identifying detail visible in frame.
scenes.first_frame_still_prompt: The same traveler's head is just settling onto the top strap of the exact reference Transit Backpack, eyes closing, as the night train rocks gently forward. Outside the dark window, neon city lights begin to blur into soft streaks, while warm cabin light falls across their face and the bag's edge, contrasting with the cool tones sliding past behind them.
scenes.S1_feeling: Guard down — trust that the bag is holding everything so they don't have to.
scenes.S2_first_frame: Head just beginning to rest on the strap, lights still sharp before they blur.
scenes.S3_one_action: One continuous action: settling into sleep against the pack as the train rocks and lights streak.
scenes.S4_new_information: Shows the product doing the thing that matters — being trustworthy enough to sleep on, mid-journey.
scenes.S5_impact: Intimate close framing keeps the product and gesture legible even in a small vertical crop.

scenes.prompt: The same traveler strides out of a station exit into a lit-up city street at dusk, wearing the exact Transit Backpack from the reference photos settled on both shoulders, moving forward with a steady, continuous stride. Camera tracks alongside at walking pace. City glow ahead, warm practicals lining the street, shallow depth of field on the background. Confident, unhurried pace. No text overlays.
scenes.first_frame_still_prompt: The traveler is captured mid-stride just as they exit the station doorway, the exact reference Transit Backpack settled evenly on both shoulders, straps secure and steady. Ahead, the city street glows with warm practical lights at dusk, the path open and inviting, while the station's threshold frames them stepping confidently forward into the scene.
scenes.S1_feeling: Steady arrival — the version of yourself that walks out after a hard journey.
scenes.S2_first_frame: First step out of the station doorway into the dusk street, pack already settled and secure.
scenes.S3_one_action: One continuous action: walking forward from the station exit into the street without breaking stride.
scenes.S4_new_information: Delivers the payoff — the traveler transformed from delayed and slumped to steady and moving, product unchanged, doing its job invisibly.
scenes.S5_impact: Clear forward motion and a lit, uncluttered street keep the payoff readable at speed on a phone.

finish.copy_placement: Headline 'Room for the long way home.' set large in the calm shadowed lower zone of the closing frame; 'Transit Backpack · 30L' smaller in caps directly beneath it; 'mokobara.com' and the logo sit at the very bottom edge. Light-on-dark type, contrast-checked against the darkest bench-shadow patch, subtle dark gradient behind the text so legibility never depends on the photo alone.
finish.end_card: Hard cut from Scene 3 to a static closing frame: the exact reference-photo Transit Backpack alone on the same wooden bench, warm dusk rim-light, headline/product name/URL/logo in the shadowed lower band. This end-card is exported directly as the 1:1 and 4:5 poster assets you asked for.
finish.music: A single sustained, low-key ambient tone under scenes 1–3 (no lyrics), settling to silence on the closing card — carries the mood without competing with the visual beats.

decisions.D1_idea: On a long transit day — delay, red-eye, arrival — the Transit Backpack is the one thing that quietly holds everything a traveler needs, so they can let their guard down and still walk out steady.
decisions.D2_conflict: A frequent domestic traveler catching late trains or red-eye connections for work is worn down by delays and cramped terminals, and worries about digging through a badly organized bag exhausted at midnight.
decisions.D3_roles: The hero is the visibly on-screen tired traveler; the brand plays the quietly capable enabler — the exact reference-photo backpack that carries them through the delay, the doze, and the walk home.
decisions.D4_opening: Scene 1: the traveler drops onto a bench beside a glowing DELAYED board, pack sliding off one shoulder — a bold, specific, mid-action opening that a thumb would stop on.
decisions.D5_brand: The exact reference-photo backpack is visible on the traveler's body in all three motion scenes (early and late), and again alone, unmarked but logo-labelled, on the closing card — recurring across more than one kind of asset (motion + static end-card) so no competitor could be credited.
decisions.D6_ask_and_end: The implicit ask is to visit mokobara.com, carried by on-screen text on the closing card; the video and the exportable poster both end on the product alone.

D7_product_truth.fact: The backpack has the exact silhouette, colour, straps and hardware shown in the 3 supplied reference photos.
The product is the Transit Backpack, 30L capacity.

decisions.D8_deviations: The brief asked for a 'launch poster' in 1:1/4:5; we deliver that literal static poster as the closing card (exportable in both ratios), but built it on top of a short 3-beat motion sequence so the idea has real tension, a visible hero, and a shown (not just stated) product moment — per the rule that a scene's moment can't be deleted or swapped for a still to pass review. Clients who only want the still can extract the end-card alone.
